what: Estée Lauder sells prestige beauty products: skin care, make-up, fragrance and hair care under Estée Lauder, Clinique, La Mer, MAC, Jo Malone, Tom Ford Beauty and other brands, in about 150 countries.
customers: Beauty shoppers in department stores, specialty retailers, travel retail at airports and online.
money: Estée Lauder, Clinique and La Mer
Jo Malone, Tom Ford and Le Labo
moat: Prestige brands with long histories and counter space in department stores worldwide, where customers return to the same product for years.
risks: Operating margin fell to about 5% as Chinese and travel retail demand collapsed
Revenue has fallen about 2% a year over three years
Chinese consumers have shifted to local beauty brands
Debt of about $9 billion while profits are depressed
opportunities: Gross margin of 76% shows the brands still command premium prices
A new chief executive is cutting costs and rebuilding the US business
Fragrance has kept growing while the rest of the portfolio has not
watch: Asia travel retail sales and whether operating margin recovers.
